record.original_question: Let R be a commutative ring, let A be a commutative R-algebra, and call an R-subspace M of A a Mathieu subspace if for any a, b in A, whenever a^m belongs to M for all sufficiently large m, one also has a^m b in M for all sufficiently large m. Let M = {f in C[x] | integral over Cn of f(x) dx = 0}. Is M a Mathieu subspace of the polynomial algebra C[x]?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Definitions. Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $A$ a commutative $R$-algebra. An $R$-subspace $M \subseteq A$ is called a Mathieu subspace of $A$ if for every $a, b \in A$ the following implication holds: whenever $a^m \in M$ for all sufficiently large positive integers $m$, one also has $a^m b \in M$ for all sufficiently large positive integers $m$.

Setup. Fix a positive integer $n$, let $C^n := [0,1]^n \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be the closed unit $n$-cube, and consider the polynomial algebra $A = \mathbb{C}[x] = \mathbb{C}[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ in $n$ variables over $\mathbb{C}$. Define the $\mathbb{C}$-linear subspace
$$ M \;:=\; \Bigl\{\, f \in \mathbb{C}[x_1,\dots,x_n] \;\Big|\; \int_{C^n} f(x)\,dx = 0 \,\Bigr\}. $$

Question. Is $M$ a Mathieu subspace of the polynomial algebra $\mathbb{C}[x_1,\dots,x_n]$? That is, does it hold that for every $f, g \in \mathbb{C}[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, if $\int_{C^n} f(x)^m\,dx = 0$ for all sufficiently large $m$, then $\int_{C^n} f(x)^m g(x)\,dx = 0$ for all sufficiently large $m$?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search for results on this specific cube-integral Mathieu subspace question did not return a definitive resolution. Subsequent work has developed Mathieu–Zhao subspaces in polynomial rings, but no source clearly confirms that this particular question (vanishing of integrals of f^m over the unit n-cube implying vanishing of integrals of f^m g) has been resolved either way; status is therefore inconclusive.
